evidence.quote: The uniform degree uses the canonical-index theorem and the relative denominator theorem below.

outputs.exact_statement: There is a positive integer $N_4$ such that $N_4K_X\sim0$ for every normal projective klt complex fourfold $X$ with $K_X\sim_\mathbb Q0$.

Let $\Phi\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$ be finite. There is a positive integer $m=m(\Phi)$ such that the following holds. Suppose $X$ is a normal integral projective complex fourfold, $\Delta\geq0$ is a rational Weil divisor whose nonzero coefficients lie in $\Phi$, $(X,\Delta)$ is lc, and $D=K_X+\Delta$ is rational Cartier and pseudo-effective. Then the complete system $|\lfloor mD\rfloor|$ is nonempty and its section ratios generate $K(D)$ inside $\mathbb C(X)$. The same integer works for every choice of canonical divisor on $X$.

Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a projective lc rational pair over $\mathbb C$ of dimension at most four, with effective boundary and nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier adjoint $D=K_X+\Delta$. If $\kappa(X,D)\ge0$, then $D$ is semiample. If $\kappa(X,D)=0$, then $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$.

Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a projective lc rational pair of dimension four over $\mathbb C$, with $D=K_X+\Delta$ $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and $\kappa(X,D)\geq0$. There is a projective $\mathbb Q$-factorial dlt pair $(X',\Delta')$ with semiample adjoint $D'=K_{X'}+\Delta'$ such that, under the identification of rational function fields and compatible canonical divisors, $$\label{eq:all-rounded-sections}
 H^0\bigl(X,\mathcal O_X(\lfloor mD\rfloor)\bigr)
 =H^0\bigl(X',\mathcal O_{X'}(\lfloor mD'\rfloor)\bigr)
 \qquad(m\geq1).$$ The coefficients of $\Delta'$ belong to those of $\Delta$ together with $1$. The map is obtained by a crepant dlt modification followed by adjoint-negative birational steps. For a $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt input the latter steps can be taken directly, with klt outputs. The semiample contraction $f:X'\to Z$ has $\dim Z=\kappa(X,D)$ and $$D'\sim_{\mathbb Q}f^*A$$ for an ample rational Cartier divisor $A$ on the normal projective variety $Z$.

Let $D$ be a rational Cartier divisor on a normal projective variety such that $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}f^*A$ for a contraction $f:X\to Z$ and an ample rational Cartier divisor $A$. If one nonempty complete system $|\lfloor mD\rfloor|$ generates $\mathbb C(Z)$ inside $\mathbb C(X)$, then every positive integer multiple of $m$ does so as well.

Fix a finite set $\Phi\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$ and an integer $1\leq d\leq4$. There are positive integers $p_0\mid p$, with $p_0$ clearing $\Phi$, and a DCC set $\mathcal B\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$, depending only on $d$ and $\Phi$, with the following property.*

*Let $(X,B)$ be a projective lc pair of dimension $d$, with effective rational boundary having coefficients in $\Phi$. Suppose that $f:X\to Z$ is a contraction onto a projective base $Z$, with $\dim Z>0$, and $$K_X+B\sim_\mathbb Qf^*D$$ for a $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor $D$ on $Z$. There exist $\psi\in\mathbb C(X)^*$ and a $\mathbb Q$-Cartier divisor $D_Z\sim_\mathbb QD$ such that $$\label{eq:relative-exact-presentation}
 K_X+B+\frac1{p_0}\mathop{\mathrm{Div}}(\psi)=f^*D_Z,
 \qquad D_Z=K_Z+B_Z+M_Z.$$ Here $B_Z$ is effective with coefficients in $\mathcal B$, $(Z,B_Z+M_Z)$ is generalized lc, and $\mathbf M$ is b-nef with $p\mathbf M$ b-Cartier. If $(X,B)$ is klt, the generalized pair on $Z$ is generalized klt.

Under the hypotheses of Theorem 6, suppose in addition that $D$ is big. There is a positive integer $m=m(d,\Phi)$ such that, for every positive multiple $l$ of $m$, the complete divisorial system $$\left|\left\lfloor l(K_X+B)\right\rfloor\right|$$ is nonempty and generates precisely the subfield $\mathbb C(Z)\subset\mathbb C(X)$. Its rational map is therefore birationally equivalent to $f$ and to the Iitaka fibration of $K_X+B$.

Fix an integer $1\leq d\leq 4$, a DCC set $I\subset [0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$, and a positive integer $p$. There exists a positive integer $\ell=\ell(d,I,p)$ with the following property. Let $Z$ be a normal projective complex variety of dimension $d$ with a rationally connected smooth projective resolution. Suppose that $(Z,B+M_Z)$ is generalized klt, that $B\geq 0$ has coefficients in $I$, and that the b-nef rational b-divisor $\mathbf M$ has $p\mathbf M$ b-Cartier. If $$D=K_Z+B+M_Z\sim_{\mathbb Q}0,$$ then $\ell D$ is an integral principal divisor. Consequently, for every integer $a\geq1$, the divisor $a\ell D$ is principal and $$h^0\bigl(Z,\mathcal O_Z(a\ell D)\bigr)=1.$$ The same integer can be chosen for all dimensions in any fixed subset of $\{1,2,3,4\}$.

There is a uniform positive integer $N_{\rm prod}$ with the following property. If a projective klt fourfold $X$, with $K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$, admits a cover as in [eq:index-product-cover] having at least two positive dimensional factors, or having only an abelian factor, then $N_{\rm prod}K_X\sim0$.

Suppose that a projective klt fourfold $X$, with $K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$, has a finite quasi-étale cover $P\to X$ in which $P$ is one four-dimensional irreducible Calabi–Yau or irreducible holomorphic symplectic factor as above. Then the following statements hold.*

1.  *There is no dominant rational map from $X$ to a positive dimensional non-uniruled smooth projective variety of dimension less than four.*

2.  *Every positive dimensional rational image of dimension less than four has rationally connected smooth projective resolution.*

3.  *Every smooth projective model of $X$ has irregularity zero.
Let $u:W\to X$ be a projective birational morphism from a smooth projective fourfold to a normal projective variety. A pseudo-effective $u$-exceptional real divisor on $W$ is effective.
The canonical orders of the noncanonical varieties in Lemma 10 are uniformly bounded.
A normal projective canonical variety $X$ with $K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$ has a projective crepant $\mathbb Q$-factorial terminalization $V\to X$. The canonical orders of $V$ and $X$ are equal.

There is a uniform positive integer $N_{\rm mov}$ with the following property. Let $V$ be a projective $\mathbb Q$-factorial terminal fourfold with $K_V\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$, and suppose that every positive dimensional rational image of dimension less than four has rationally connected smooth projective resolution. If $V$ has an effective Weil divisor $D$ with $1\le\kappa(V,D)\le3$, then $N_{\rm mov}K_V\sim0$.

Let $V$ be a projective $\mathbb Q$-factorial terminal fourfold with $K_V\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$. Suppose that every effective Weil divisor on $V$ of positive Iitaka dimension is big. Let $\pi:Y\to V$ be its cyclic index cover, with deck group $G$. Then every $G$-equivariant rational fibration of $Y$ with positive dimensional base and fibre has a geometric generic fibre of general type on a smooth resolution. The same conclusion holds for every such rational fibration of $V$.

Let a nonempty finite list of marked covering families be given on an integral projective variety $V$ in characteristic zero. There is a dominant rational map $$\xi:V\dashrightarrow M$$ with geometrically integral generic fibre, whose fibre closures $H_p\ni p$ have a constant positive dimension $e$ for general $p$. Starting at a generic $p$, a path of at most $e$ generic movements reaches a point generic in $H_p$ over the algebraic closure of the field of $p$. Every generic movement preserves the value of $\xi$. In particular, a generic family member $C_b$ is contained in $H_{u(b)}$.*

*The assignment is equivariant under any finite automorphism group preserving the family list.

Suppose a dominant rational map between two ambient varieties sends generic movements of an upper family list to generic movements of a lower family list, or to stationary steps. Then the image of a generic upper leaf is contained in the corresponding lower leaf.*

*If a finite group preserves a family list on $V$ and $\theta:V\to V'$ is its quotient, the subvarieties $\theta(H_p)$ are the closures of the geometrically integral generic fibres of a rational fibration on $V'$.

Let the marked families and their rational quotient be as in Lemma 16, and let $e$ be the dimension of a generic leaf. Suppose that $P$ is a big, nef, semiample rational Cartier divisor on $V$. Assume that, for every family, its geometric generic marked member satisfies one of the following bounds, with a common number $B\ge0$:* 1. *the mark is smooth on $C_b$ and $\gamma(P;C_b,u(b))\le B$;* 2. *$C_b$ is a curve and $P\cdot C_b/\mathop{\mathrm{mult}}_{u(b)}C_b\le B$.* *Then on the geometric generic leaf, $$\label{eq:chain-order-degree} \gamma(P;H_p)\le eB, \qquad P^e\cdot H_p\le(eB)^e.$$

Let $X$ be a projective variety birational to a smooth projective variety with a nonzero pluricanonical section. A smooth projective resolution of the geometric generic member of a covering family of integral subvarieties of $X$ has nonnegative Kodaira dimension. If $X$ is of general type, that resolution is of general type.

Let $X$ be a normal projective canonical fourfold over $\mathbb C$ with $K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$, and let $r$ be the least positive integer such that $rK_X\sim0$. Let $\pi:Y\to X$ be its canonical cyclic cover, with group $\mu_r$. Fix $C_1\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$, and choose $b_0\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$ satisfying $$\label{eq:frob-choice-b0} 3(2b_0)^4<\frac14, \qquad b_0(C_1+1)<\frac34.$$ Suppose that $L$ is an ample rational Cartier divisor on $X$ such that $$1\le L^4\le2, \qquad \gamma(L;X)\le C_1,$$ where $\gamma$ is as in Definition 18. For each integer $t\ge2$, set $$Z_t=Y^t/\mu_{r,\mathrm{diag}}, \qquad \theta_t:Z_t\longrightarrow X^t, \qquad P_t=\theta_t^*\left(\sum_{i=1}^t\operatorname{pr}_i^*L\right).$$ Then $P_t$ is ample and, at a very general point $z$ of $Z_t$, $$\label{eq:frob-cost} \varepsilon(P_t;z)\le\frac{5t^2}{b_0}.$$

Let $C$ be a smooth projective integral curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $V$ be a vector bundle of rank $n$ with $\mu_{\min}(V)\ge0$, and put $$G=\max\{0,2g-2\},\qquad u=n(p-1),\qquad c_2=n(n-1)G.$$ Let $A_\bullet(V)$ denote the symmetric algebra of $V$ modulo the ideal locally generated by the $p$-th powers of its linear generators. Thus, in a local frame, $A_\bullet(V)$ is the graded algebra $\mathcal O_C[v_1,\ldots,v_n]/(v_1^p,\ldots,v_n^p)$. Its graded pieces are locally free, it is zero in degrees above $u$, and $$\label{eq:frob-truncated-upper-slope}
 \mu_{\max}\bigl(A_j(V)\bigr)
 \le (p-1)\deg(V)+c_2
 \qquad (0\le j\le u).$$

Let $W$ be a smooth projective fourfold over an algebraically closed field, and let $H$ be an ample rational Cartier divisor. Fix a smooth complete intersection flag, cut successively by divisors from $|l_1H|$, $|l_2H|$, and $|l_3H|$, ending in a smooth integral curve $C$; here each $l_iH$ is an integral ample divisor. Write $d_i=l_iH\cdot C$. If $E$ is a vector bundle of rank $e$ and $\mu_{\max}(E|_C)\le M$ for a real number $M\ge0$, then $$\label{eq:frob-flag-sections}
 h^0(W,E)\le e(M+1)\prod_{i=1}^3\left(1+\frac{M}{d_i}\right).$$

For $1\le i\le t$, let $V_i$ be an integral projective variety over an algebraically closed field, let $x_i\in V_i$ be a smooth point, and let $M_i$ be a line bundle with $H^0(V_i,M_i)\ne0$. Put $$a_i=\max_{0\ne s\in H^0(V_i,M_i)}\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_{x_i}(s).$$ Every nonzero section $s$ of the external product $\bigotimes_i\operatorname{pr}_i^*M_i$ satisfies $$\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_{(x_1,\ldots,x_t)}(s)\le\sum_{i=1}^t a_i.$$

Let $X$ be a normal projective terminal variety with $K_X\sim_\mathbb Q0$. If a smooth projective resolution of $X$ has irregularity zero, then $\mathop{\mathrm{Bir}}(X)$ is countable.
